Ordered implementation recommendations

The dependency graph is: discovery independently; task semantics plus adapter mechanisms feed canonical execution; policy develops against verified mock declarations; execution and policy join across every acceptance transition; conduct then composes discovery, enforced delegation and measured adapters. Live diagnostics provide admission evidence. Contract acceptance permits independent construction; it is not runtime activation.

The file ownership below is exclusive implementation ownership. Each listed multi-part unit is split into buckets of at most three files. One producer owns each shared file throughout integration; later phases on that file are sequential. Independent producers own tests, fixtures and their review. New API names and test filenames below are proposed interfaces to freeze before authoring, not claims that they exist.

1. Freeze only the missing executable seams.

Bucket 1a owns additions to ops/conductor/lane-policy.md, ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md and ops/devlane/task/CONTRACT.md. Specify trusted transport for selection, requested scope, declaration provenance, dependency evidence, output/attempt receipts and result.policy. Preserve existing brief.policy structure. Reserve the dispatch identifier in memory before validating job-bound evidence; create no attempt or filesystem state before the required admission checks. Specify late refusal serialization separately from prelaunch refusal.

Bucket 1b owns conductor-start-plan.md, harness-capabilities.md and permission-surface.md; bucket 1c owns the bounded probes-lever.md extension. Freeze the conductor launch descriptor, safe argv grammar, normalized tool-request interface, live observation format and diagnostic bootstrap. Retain the independent doctor and permitted coordination reads. Do not turn the old unarmed conductor guard into authority.

These are small interface completions, not another discovery design or whole-lane audit. No new profile key in lane.conf, policy registry, execution store, writable MCP tool or generic workflow implementation is needed. Acceptance: git diff --check plus independent schema/example and owning-link review. These commands establish contract consistency only.

Keep acquisition outside the subprocess-free core; preserve v1/v2 bytes. Trusted launch supplies conductor-only sources, anchors and bindings.
